comment: Notary payload-signing vectors exercised through the live SDK signer: arkret-rust-sdk/crates/signatures/src/signer.rs::Ed25519PayloadSigner + verify_ed25519_payload_signature. Validates the deterministic-vs-ephemeral seed contract: (a) a configured 32-byte seed is byte-deterministic (same seed + same canonical body => same detached-JWS signature segment) so notary signatures replay across restart; (b) an ephemeral seed is non-deterministic because the seed is fresh randomness; (c) different seeds produce different signatures for the same canonical body (key binding); (d) the signature round-trips through verify_ed25519_payload_signature with the signer-derived verifying key; (e) PayloadSignature.payload_digest equals sha256 of the canonical body bytes. Unlike the earlier structural-only revision, cotest now runs real ed25519 operations against the SDK types for every vector, so the suite fails loudly if the SDK signer contract moves.

expected.rationale: Configured 32-byte seed + same canonical body bytes => identical Ed25519 signature on every invocation. The detached-JWS signature segment and payload_digest are byte-stable, which is what lets a notary replay its own notary signatures across a restart. Cotest constructs two signers from the same seed and asserts the two PayloadSignature.jws strings are equal.

An ephemeral seed is fresh CSPRNG bytes per signer construction, so each run holds a different signing key. Even with identical canonical body bytes the JWS signature segment differs. Suitable for one-shot fixtures and ephemeral peers; MUST NOT back a notary that needs restart-replay. Cotest draws two independent random seeds and asserts the signatures differ.

Key binding: s = sign(sk, m). Same m, distinct sk => distinct s. Confirms Ed25519PayloadSigner is not silently reusing a process-global key; each signer carries its own SigningKey derived from its own seed. payload_digest, by contrast, MUST be identical across the two signers because it commits only to the canonical body.

Round trip: signer.sign_payload(m) => PayloadSignature; verify_ed25519_payload_signature(m, sig, signer.verifying_key()) returns Ok(()). The verifying key comes from the same SigningKey, so the loop closes without a DID-resolver dependency.

PayloadSignature.payload_digest = sha256:<hex of canonical body>. A receiver re-derives the canonical body bytes and recomputes sha256; it must equal the declared payload_digest before the JWS signature segment is verified. Wire-form invariant for detached JWS (RFC 7515 section 3.2). Cotest asserts the SDK-produced digest equals the fixture-pinned digest, so the fixture pin and the SDK cannot drift apart silently.

Verifying with a key derived from a different seed => the signature does not validate. Ed25519 is non-malleable; the verifier MUST reject. Cotest signs with the vector seed and calls verify_ed25519_payload_signature with the drift seed's verifying key, asserting Err.

After signing, an attacker mutates the canonical body bytes. The payload_digest carried in PayloadSignature no longer matches sha256(tampered_body), so verify_ed25519_payload_signature MUST reject on the digest comparison before it ever touches the JWS signature segment.
